stages.title: Asymmetric information and regulation
stages.sub: Why regulators struggle to control firms they know less about than the firms know about themselves.

steps.q: A water company's managers know exactly what their pipes cost to run and maintain. The regulator setting price rules only sees the reports the company chooses to send. Who knows more about the firm's true costs?
steps.hint: Think about who actually works inside the firm every day versus who reads its paperwork once a year.

steps.right: It becomes hard to get the cap right
steps.wrong: It stays just as easy to get right

steps.q: Price caps, profit caps and quality standards all rely on the regulator knowing the truth about the firm. If the firm always knows more than the regulator, can any of these tools ever be fully reliable?
steps.right: No, all of them stay imperfect
steps.wrong: Yes, at least one can be made fully reliable
